title: infrastructure-weekly-update-2026-05-25
summary: Weekly update covering GPU fleet health, region capacity planning, upcoming maintenance, and action items for autoscaling and billing optimization.
content:
TL;DR: Fleet steady overall. H100 rollouts in us-west1 on track (50/120 nodes live); temporary capacity pressure observed in eu-west1 due to a spike in eval jobs — short-term burst handled via spot pools and cross-region routing. Next week focus: finalize H100 onboarding playbook, implement soft quotas for large eval jobs, and confirm maintenance window for kernel upgrades (2026-06-02).

1) Current fleet snapshot (2026-05-24 23:00 UTC)
- Total GPUs by type (logical): H100: 620 (120 in us-west1 live; 200 provisioning in ap-southeast1; remainder in staging), A100: 840, T4: 410.
- Available capacity (estimate): global available H100 cores approx 18% idle, A100 approx 22% idle, T4 approx 35% idle.
- Spot pool sizes: us-west1 spot H100 pool ~40 nodes (usable), eu-west1 spot A100 pool ~30 nodes.

2) Regions 
- us-west1: H100 rollout continuing. 50 new H100 nodes were validated and promoted to production this week. Median p95 latency unchanged. Observed kernel panic on 1 node; automated repro and replacement worked as expected. Next: scaling policy bump for H100 pool from 100 -> 140 planned after QA.
- eu-west1: Capacity tight this Wednesday during a large internal eval run (team: applied-ml). Queuing for latency-sensitive hosted API increased for 12 minutes before cross-region routing diverted noncritical batch jobs. Action: set up soft quotas for internal evals to prevent future impact.
- ap-southeast1: Additional A100/H100 racks provisioning. Networking ACL change required for onboarding — Diego is coordinating Rack Ops.

3) Incidents & Reliability
- Incident INF-2026-0519: Increased queuing in eu-west1 for 12 minutes. Root cause: multiple large eval clusters launched without cluster-size caps. Mitigation: automated reroute + manual cancellation of lower-priority jobs. Postmortem draft linked in Confluence.
- Minor: 1 kernel panic in us-west1 (see above) — auto-replace worked. No customer-facing impact.

4) Capacity planning / forecasting
- Short-term (next 2 weeks): expected reduction in A100 demand due to internal training cadence finishing May 28; expected increase in H100 global demand as we onboard new customers who specified low-latency configs.
- Mid-term (next 2–3 months): projected 18% fleet growth to support Dedicated capacity commitments; finance requested conservative cost estimate vs. expected revenue — meeting scheduled with FP&A 2026-05-27.
- Action: finalize H100 provisioning runway by EOD 2026-05-29 (Jordan). Include estimated lead times for additional power/cooling at on-prem partner sites.

5) Autoscaling & Scheduling
- Continuous batching improvements merged (PR #678). Early results: 6–9% throughput improvement for large seq workloads.
- Autoscaler issue: occasional thrashing observed when scaling H100 pools under bursty load. Root cause likely threshold hysteresis. Plan: increase scale-down cooldown and introduce a scaling buffer for H100 nodes. Diego to propose tuning by 2026-05-28.

6) Cost & Billing notes
- Spot utilization saved ~12% of GPU spend last week; however, preemption rate for some workloads spiked in us-west1 on 2026-05-21 causing ~1.8% extra job rerun cost.
- Optimize: schedule non-latency eval jobs to eu-west1 overnight to take advantage of lower spot contention. Ops to publish recommended scheduling tags for internal teams.

7) Operational items / maintenance
- Kernel upgrade window: 2026-06-02 02:00–06:00 UTC. Target: apply vendor kernel patch and CUDA driver 12.3.3. Expect rolling reboots of 10–15% capacity per region; will enable cross-region routing to avoid customer impact.
- Node decommission plan: retire oldest A100 rack in us-east1 starting 2026-06-10 after replacement inventory arrives.

8) Roadmap / upcoming work
- H100 onboarding playbook: final draft due 2026-05-29. Includes validation tests, kernel/driver matrix, thermal checks, and rollback steps. Owner: Avery.
- Autoscaler tuning RFC: publish 2026-05-27. Owner: Diego.
- Quota system for internal eval clusters: prototype by 2026-06-04. Owner: Samira.

9) Action items (owners + due dates)
- Jordan: Complete provisioning runway doc + lead-time table (due 2026-05-29).
- Diego: Autoscaler tuning proposal (due 2026-05-28).
- Samira: Quota prototype for eval clusters and tagging guidance for teams (due 2026-06-04).
- Avery: Publish H100 onboarding playbook (due 2026-05-29).
- Ops: Publish scheduling tags for non-latency workloads (due 2026-05-27).

10) Notes / open questions
- Can Finance approve a short-term burst credit for A100/spot overages during onboarding to avoid throttling customer workloads? (FP&A meeting 2026-05-27)
- Do we want to enforce hard caps on internal eval clusters or prefer soft quotas + alerts? Ops leaning to soft quotas first.

Meeting attendees: Avery Chen, Jordan Patel, Samira Khan, Diego Morales, Priya Gupta (SRE), Marco Liu (Applied ML), 10 attendees total.

Appendix: quick logs/snippets
- Kernel panic log snippet (us-west1 node-42): "kernel: BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer deref at 0000000000000000" — auto-replacement triggered.
- Autoscaler thrash trace: scaling down H100 pool twice within 9 minutes during a burst; cooldown was 120s. Proposed cooldown = 600s.

If anything looks off or you want expanded metrics (per-tenant usage, per-model tail latency), I can add those to next week's note.
